Maya (arch): FYI spotted weird credential fanout when hosted falls back to dedicated during a zone outage. tokens that should be short-lived are getting replayed across adapters.
Sam (eng-runtime): oof. do you have a minimal repro?
Maya (arch): small one. calling a pinned model on hosted, sim outage -> routed to dedicated fallback -> dedicated proxy rebinds tenant token to worker pool and we see the same token in logs for different tenant requests.
Jordan (eng-platform): can you paste the log snippet?
Maya (arch): sure — trimmed:```
[2026-03-21T16:12:03Z] route=hosted->dedicated fallback, tenant=acme-corp, token=tok-abc123
[2026-03-21T16:12:04Z] worker=pool-7 handling request, auth=tok-abc123, request_id=R1
[2026-03-21T16:12:05Z] worker=pool-7 handling request, auth=tok-abc123, request_id=R2
```
Sam (eng-runtime): looks like the adapter cached the token as part of the affinity slot. We expected the proxy to re-scope to a per-request short token but it's keeping the original.
Lucas (sec): if that's true, blast radius is big. tokens should be bound to session or context id. caching per affinity without tenant isolation is a violation.
Anna (product): do customers see data leaking or just audit noise?
Maya (arch): so far audit noise + confusing billing attribution. We haven't detected cross-tenant payload leaks, but logs show token reuse across requests that belong to different calling sessions.
Jordan (eng-platform): quick design idea: split affinity key from credential binding. affinity -> routing hint only, credential store -> ephemeral per-request rebind using KMS. That way the cache doesn't hold raw tokens.
Sam (eng-runtime): implementation nit: we already have an affinity cache keyed by (model, zone, tenant) -> worker. Adding a layer that stores only a credential handle (opaque id) rather than token might be doable. but we need to ensure handle lifetime is short.
Lucas (sec): handles must be bound to a capability and TTL. Also require audit token exchange: the dedicated side should emit an audit event when it accepts a handle and resolves it to a token.
Maya (arch): agree. another wrinkle: private deployments where customer-managed KMS is used — we can't perform rebind ourselves. We need a contract: private adapter must implement a token-exchange endpoint.
Jordan (eng-platform): that contract could be a minimal HTTP endpoint: `/v1/exchange-handle` expecting handle+context and returning short token. sketch:```
POST /v1/exchange-handle
{ handle: "h-xyz", ctx: { request_id: "R1", route: "fallback" } }
=> { token: "s-tok", expires_at: "..." }
```
Anna (product): must be optional for hosted/dedicated combos where we control KMS. For private, we require it during onboarding. Should be in the private deployment checklist.
Sam (eng-runtime): performance concern: extra roundtrip on every request kills p95. We can batch exchanges or do a short-lived local cache of exchanged tokens keyed by request fingerprint. But that brings us back to cache eviction correctness.
Maya (arch): proposal: two-mode flow:
- fast-path: hosted->dedicated same control plane: runtime returns a short-scoped token directly (no extra hop)
- gated-path: hosted->private or hosted->dedicated when controlplane cannot rebind: use `exchange-handle` with aggressively short TTL and per-worker sandboxing.
Lucas (sec): also add a deterministic way to tag tokens with `origin` and `scope-id` so audit can show whether a token came from handle exchange or from original credential.
Jordan (eng-platform): operationally we'll need metric windows: `handle_exchange_rate`, `handle_cache_hit`, `token_rebind_errors`. deploy-bot: new metric alerts created: infra#metrics/handle_exchange_rate >= 10/s for 5m.
deploy-bot: deployment notice: adding feature flag `runtime.credential_exchange_v2` to rollout.
Sam (eng-runtime): implementation steps I see:
1) change affinity cache value to { worker, cred_handle_id }
2) introduce cred-exchange client with pluggable adapter endpoint
3) audit events + TTL enforcement in worker
4) perf tests (p95 baseline) and a canary rollout behind flag
Maya (arch): sounds good. questions: how do we expire cred_handle across restarts? store in memstore with TTL + persistent lease?
Jordan (eng-platform): use existing lease service: put handle -> lease with TTL. on restart, worker must re-fetch or fail closed.
Lucas (sec): fail-closed is critical. If handle cannot be resolved, reject request with 401, do not fallback silently.
Anna (product): timeline expectation? customers with private deployments need docs and checklist in the next 2 sprints.
Sam (eng-runtime): dev plan: spike this week, PR next week, canary in two weeks. I'll own runtime changes. Jordan can handle platform bits. Maya will sign off on design.
Maya (arch): cool. I'll merge this thread into the design doc and add a short diagram. thanks all. :pray:
Lucas (sec): add a short threat-model section please.
Jordan (eng-platform): noted. I'll also add the metrics and alert entries to runbook.
Maya (arch): closing notes: avoid storing raw tokens anywhere outside KMS boundary; treat affinity as routing only. keep exchange minimal and auditable.
Sam (eng-runtime): ack. will raise follow-up if perf gets worse.
Anna (product): ping me before docs update for customer messaging.
deploy-bot: milestone created: credential-exchange-v2 (owner: sam).
